sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:1
items.html: Two kinds of reflected light are discerned immediately at the time of the coupling by striking. The first is the light that is rejected from expanding into the vessel of Malchut, by reason of the striking of the screen, and this reflected light is discerned as surrounding light. The second is the reflected light that is born through the shared relation of the discernment of the departure and the withdrawal of phase four from the light, which joins with the said rejected light; and it is the reflected light that ascends from below upward and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light of the Rosh [head].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:2
items.html: The third kind is the fixed reflected light in Malchut of the Rosh [head], which is made there as a source from which the lights and the vessels are bestowed and flow to the Guf [body].

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:3
items.html: The fourth kind is the reflected light that expands from Malchut of the Rosh downward and draws and clothes the ten Sefirot of direct light that expand with it. And this reflected light is discerned as being mixed with the direct light, and it is not recognised as a garment and a vessel, because its importance is equal to that of the direct light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:4
items.html: The fifth kind is the minute illumination of direct light that is bestowed below the Tabur, which is called female light. And it too is called reflected light.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:5
items.html: The sixth kind is the reflected light that concludes each and every Sefira of the ten Sefirot that are from the Tabur downward, until it concludes the whole Partzuf.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:6
items.html: The seventh kind is the reflected light that is called coarse light, which remains below without light after the departure of the direct light. For then the coarseness in its own essence is discernible, from the aspect of what had been included in it even before it expanded from the Peh [mouth] downward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:7
items.html: The eighth kind is reflected light to which a doubled coarseness was added upon its coarseness, because it remained after the departure below without light. And this darkness that it has now acquired is a new coarseness, which was not in it before it expanded from the Peh downward.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:8
items.html: The ninth kind is the direct light in the levels that emerge at the time of the refining, which is considered reflected light and judgement because they emerge at a time of departure.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:9
items.html: The tenth kind is the reflected light that descends from the illumination of the coupling in the upper phase to the vessel beneath her, which is empty of its light, and which comes into a coupling by striking with the record that is there in that vessel.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:10
items.html: The eleventh kind is the sparks that fall into the vessels, which were separated out from the said descending reflected light, and which prevailed over the record because the illumination of the coupling shines upon them.

items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 21:11
items.html: The twelfth kind is the said sparks after they have been extinguished — that is, after the illumination of the coupling has departed from the upper phase, for the record then prevails over them. (Inner Observation, Part 4, Item 7)
